newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends down on fund spreads, late hedges.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends down on fund spreads, late hedges.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended down as funds rolled July positions into back months and on late hedges, traders said.

"The funds are rolling their July positions to August and November. There were closing hedges in the July. XCan was selling and Cargill bought November and January," a trader said. July WCE futures crush margin fell to -1.69 Wednesday from +1.93 Tuesday. About 700 July-Nov spread $33, 200 July Aug $1.60. Volume was 5,305 lots with 475 hedge lots.
July canola fell $2.50 to close at $396.20 and November slipped $1.50 to $363.20.

July flax broke ranks with canola and soy complex futures in Chicago, ending $3.20 higher at $332.90 on commercial demand, traders said. RBC-DS sold 300 November unchanged at $311, sources said. July-Nov $21.

July western barley lost $1.70 to set a new low at $128 on commercial long liquidation, floor sources said. Midland Walwyn sold December down $0.80 at $133, traders said, and Alberta Wheat Pool sold 100 July-Oct at $2.50 to RBC-DS.
July feed wheat lost $1 to $154 on commission selling, with October falling $1 to settle at $157.50. July-Oct spread at $3, July-Dec $3.50.

Louis Dreyfus sold December feed pea contracts down US$3.30 to US$174.70, traders said. UGG sold 80 Oct-May at US$1 and RBC-DS sold October and December oats down the US$5 limit to US$107 and US$109 respectively for a commercial, traders said.
(All prices in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats, peas).
